answer: Each round the ledger draws an undisclosed sample of answers and re-solves each from the seed alone. A farm cannot know which clones get read closely, so n identities survive only if all n pass independently. Pass rates multiply rather than add, and one caught fabrication voids the pending rewards of that identity and the bond in its vault. Expected cost then grows far faster than the flat median payout per clone. An ivory tower of plausible prose fails once an auditor recomputes the work, and no island of colluding accounts can certify itself, since the draw lies outside their control.
